Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7941); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor:--strong drink.
BiblicalUsage: Sikera is strong drink, fermented liquor, and it appears once, in the angel's word about John the Baptist before he was born: he shall drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost even from his mother's womb.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe John's abstinence was a sign, not a rule, marking the man who would prepare the way as one set apart from his birth.
